nodes.label: Insurance, Healthcare & Protection Planning (Shelter Bay)
nodes.rationale: Chapter framing: protect the downside before pursuing higher-risk upside; covers insurance layers, plan trade-offs, Medicare/Medicaid/private, and life-stage planning.

nodes.label: Investing, Markets & Portfolio Strategy (Market Straits)
nodes.rationale: Chapter framing: moves from saving to deploying capital, turning investing into a repeatable process built on risk, time horizon, valuation, and behavior.

nodes.label: Life, Morality, Meaning & Legacy (Legacy Summit)
nodes.rationale: Final chapter zooms from tactics to meaning: wealth is a tool, and the highest return is a life lived with purpose, stewardship, and fewer regrets.

nodes.label: Top Alternative Income Ideas Outside 9-to-5
nodes.rationale: Defines what makes a side-income idea good (low startup cost, clear need, repeatable demand, good margins, scalable delivery) before scoring eight ideas; validate with one paying customer before building.

nodes.label: Digital Products / Templates (highest-margin idea)
nodes.rationale: Create once, sell many; keeps 80-95% of what you sell, singled out as highest margin.

nodes.label: Five-Step Launch Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Pick one niche problem, validate with a paying customer, build a repeatable offer, systematize marketing/delivery, reinvest into growth.

nodes.label: Top Income Streams for Anyone in Life
nodes.rationale: Treats income as a ladder from labor to passive, scores ten streams on scalability/resilience, and argues for a mix matched to life stage.
nodes.norm_label: top income streams for anyone in life

nodes.label: The Income Ladder (labor to royalty/passive)
nodes.rationale: Five rungs: labor, skill-based, business, investment, royalty/passive income.

nodes.label: The Smart Income Mix by Life Stage
nodes.rationale: Build base income, add one skill stream, convert surplus to assets, add ownership/portfolio income, buy back time; best-fit shifts 20s to 50s+.
nodes.norm_label: the smart income mix by life stage

nodes.label: Coverage vs. Cost Trade-Offs in Insurance
nodes.rationale: Premium and out-of-pocket move in opposite directions; choosing a metal tier is really a forecast of expected usage.
nodes.norm_label: coverage vs. cost trade-offs in insurance

nodes.label: ACA Metal Tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum)
nodes.rationale: Actuarial values ~60/70/80/90%; Silver often best value when subsidy-eligible.

nodes.label: HDHP + HSA (triple-tax-advantaged pairing)
nodes.rationale: High deductible plus tax-advantaged HSA; rewards low-usage households who can cash-flow expenses; 2025 limits $4,300 self / $8,550 family.

nodes.label: Health Insurance Costs in the United States
nodes.rationale: Four cost layers (premium, deductible, copays/coinsurance, out-of-pocket max) stack in order; who pays more depends on usage pattern.
nodes.norm_label: health insurance costs in the united states

nodes.label: Four Health-Cost Layers
nodes.rationale: Premium keeps coverage, deductible paid first, copays/coinsurance shared, out-of-pocket max caps yearly cost with plan paying 100% after.

nodes.label: Healthcare Planning by Age & Life Stage
nodes.rationale: Priorities shift across four bands from 20s foundation to 65+ Medicare; the 65+ band is most procedural because enrollment carries penalties.
nodes.norm_label: healthcare planning by age & life stage

nodes.label: Medicare Enrollment & Part B
nodes.rationale: Eligibility generally at 65; Part B required to avoid late-enrollment penalties; 2025 premium $185/month.

nodes.label: Insurance Protection Stack
nodes.rationale: Five layers in priority order (health, disability, term life, property/liability, umbrella) sized against an income baseline; Big Rule: insure catastrophic loss, not routine costs.

nodes.label: Coverage Sizing Rules of Thumb
nodes.rationale: Term life ~10x income (~$1.27M at baseline), disability ~60% of pre-tax income (~$6,369/month), umbrella $1M+.

nodes.label: Medicare vs. Medicaid vs. Private Insurance
nodes.rationale: Three systems don't compete for the same people; eligibility (age, income, employment, disability) decides which applies, with dual eligibility for some.
nodes.norm_label: medicare vs. medicaid vs. private insurance

nodes.label: Dual Eligibility (Medicare + Medicaid)
nodes.rationale: Some qualify for both programs at once, unlocking extra help and lower out-of-pocket costs.

nodes.label: Asset Allocation & Diversification
nodes.rationale: Splits portfolio construction into two questions: how much risk given time horizon (allocation ladder) and what job each asset does (diversification roles).

nodes.label: The Allocation Ladder (Ultra Growth to Conservative)
nodes.rationale: Five profiles from 90/10/0 (Ultra Growth) to 40/55/5 (Conservative); rebalance band about 5 percentage points.
nodes.norm_label: the allocation ladder (ultra growth to conservative)

nodes.label: Asset Location Strategy
nodes.rationale: Distinct from allocation: which account holds which asset. Tax-deferred absorbs bonds/REITs, Roth gets highest-growth, taxable holds low-turnover ETFs; allocation comes first.

nodes.label: Building an Algorithmic Trading Model
nodes.rationale: A trading system is a five-stage pipeline (universe, data, signals, risk, execution), not one model; robustness beats curve fitting and no edge lasts forever.

nodes.label: Backtesting Checklist
nodes.rationale: Train/test split, walk-forward, out-of-sample validation, realistic slippage/fees, key metrics, benchmark vs S&P 500 / Nasdaq 100 / Dow.

nodes.label: Decoding George Tritch's Periods to Make Money
nodes.rationale: 19th-century market-cycle framework (A panic, B good times, C hard times) read as a sentiment lens, not a timing law; all-season systematic investing is the practical takeaway.
nodes.norm_label: decoding george tritch's periods to make money

nodes.label: George Tritch
nodes.rationale: Named originator of the cycle framework.

nodes.label: Samuel Benner
nodes.rationale: Historical figure closely associated with the Tritch cycle framework.

nodes.label: Optimized Selling Cycles & Timing for Stocks
nodes.rationale: Gives selling the same staged structure as buying via a Selling Ladder and Sell Signal Decision Matrix; a written exit thesis removes emotional decisions.
nodes.norm_label: optimized selling cycles & timing for stocks

nodes.label: Tax-Aware Selling
nodes.rationale: Hold over 1 year for long-term rates, offset gains with losses up to $3,000 with carryforward, spread sales across tax years.

nodes.label: Peak Times to Buy & Sell Stock Market Equities
nodes.rationale: Framework for reading market regimes via five forces (valuation, trend, liquidity, sentiment, earnings) and a signal dashboard; process beats prediction.
nodes.norm_label: peak times to buy & sell stock market equities

nodes.label: The Signal Dashboard (six indicators)
nodes.rationale: Forward P/E, earnings revisions, 200-day MA, advance/decline breadth, VIX/fear-greed, Fed/liquidity read bullish/neutral/caution.

nodes.label: Portfolio Rebalancing
nodes.rationale: Rebalancing is risk control, not timing; drift trigger ~5 points (80/20 to 88/12); rebalance in tax-advantaged accounts first.

nodes.label: Top Key Financial Indicators to Track for a Stock
nodes.rationale: Triangulate five indicator families (growth, profitability, financial strength, valuation, market behavior); quality and price are separate axes.
nodes.norm_label: top key financial indicators to track for a stock

nodes.label: Valuation vs Quality Map
nodes.rationale: Four zones; the value trap (weak quality + cheap) is the most expensive mistake.

nodes.label: Biggest Life Regrets People Commonly Have
nodes.rationale: Regret scorecard: relationships, overwork, playing safe, unspoken feelings, delayed living; time is the real wealth, and people regret waiting.
nodes.norm_label: biggest life regrets people commonly have

nodes.label: Die with Zero
nodes.rationale: Optimize, don't maximize: match money to life stage since life energy is finite; over-saving is a real cost.

nodes.rationale: Five-document stack (will, POA, healthcare directive, beneficiary designations, optional revocable trust); titles and beneficiary forms can override a will. 2025: $19,000 gift exclusion, $13.99M estate exemption.

nodes.label: Optimizing Life for Money, Health, Meaning & Happiness
nodes.norm_label: optimizing life for money, health, meaning & happiness

nodes.label: Five life pillars — money is one of five
nodes.rationale: Money, Body, Mind, Relationships, and Spirit/meaning are five equally-weighted pillars; neglecting the other four eventually undermines wealth because balance and consistency compound while intensity in one pillar does not.
nodes.norm_label: five life pillars — money is one of five

nodes.label: Flexibility beats precision in FIRE
nodes.rationale: Your FIRE number starts from expenses not salary, and a plan that only barely works is fragile; variable spending, cash buffers, multiple buckets, and the option to earn again reduce fragility. Retiring into a meaningful life matters more than the number itself.

nodes.label: Top Key Life Lessons & Morals to Live By
nodes.norm_label: top key life lessons & morals to live by

nodes.label: Values checklist — build assets, live below means
nodes.rationale: Character, relationships, growth, money/work, and inner peace are five reinforcing domains resting on integrity, stewardship, gratitude, and service. Discipline beats motivation, consistency beats intensity, and one should build assets not only income while treating time as the scarce resource.
nodes.norm_label: values checklist — build assets, live below means

nodes.label: Purpose, Money Mindset & Behavioral Finance (Mindset Cove)
nodes.norm_label: purpose, money mindset & behavioral finance (mindset cove)

nodes.label: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
nodes.norm_label: a random walk down wall street

nodes.label: Low-cost indexing and staying invested
nodes.rationale: Markets are hard to beat consistently, so broad diversification, low fees, and patience beat clever forecasting; asset allocation drives most long-term returns and the biggest avoidable threats are high fees, frequent trading, and reacting to headlines.

nodes.label: Start imperfectly with honesty about your numbers
nodes.rationale: Getting serious about money needs honesty about actual numbers and a workable plan, not perfection or high income. A starter emergency cushion and spending plan come before aggressive debt payoff or investing, and shame/avoidance are active obstacles that worsen outcomes.
nodes.norm_label: start imperfectly with honesty about your numbers

nodes.label: Money decisions are emotional; self-awareness and values first
nodes.rationale: Money decisions are emotional first, so self-awareness is a prerequisite for better choices; wealth is a tool serving a meaningful life, calm planning is the antidote to scarcity-driven decisions, and one must not confuse self-worth with net worth.
nodes.norm_label: money decisions are emotional; self-awareness and values first

nodes.label: Foundations first — cash flow, credit, save early
nodes.rationale: A financial life is built on habits — cash-flow awareness, careful credit use, saving early — not investing sophistication. The ordered playbook (open accounts, track cash flow, build reserve, clear toxic debt, automate) fails if automation is reached before a reserve exists; the goal is control, not complexity.
nodes.norm_label: foundations first — cash flow, credit, save early

nodes.label: Simple systems and consistent habits beat jargon
nodes.rationale: Everyday financial confidence comes from simple repeatable systems, not mastering jargon. The sequential playbook (budget, automate savings, improve credit, invest, review) assumes each step is in place, and small debts left unaddressed compound quickly through interest.
nodes.norm_label: simple systems and consistent habits beat jargon

nodes.label: Money is a tool; every choice is a trade-off; enough is personal
nodes.rationale: Money is a tool for building a good life, not the measure of one. Every financial decision is a trade-off, 'enough' is a personal values-based definition, and chasing status or measuring success only by net worth erodes the freedom money should buy.
nodes.norm_label: money is a tool; every choice is a trade-off; enough is personal

nodes.label: I Will Teach You to Be Rich
nodes.norm_label: i will teach you to be rich

nodes.label: Automation beats willpower; conscious spending
nodes.rationale: Systems that run on their own beat relying on willpower; conscious spending means cutting mercilessly on what you don't value to spend extravagantly on what you do. Big wins (fees, savings rate, debt, negotiation) outrank small hacks, and simple low-cost investing is sufficient.

nodes.label: Assets vs liabilities; cash flow builds wealth
nodes.rationale: Assets put money in your pocket while liabilities take money out, and confusing the two is the most common financial mistake. Positive cash flow (not income size) is the goal, financial literacy is a prerequisite skill, and the book is a mindset shift rather than literal doctrine.
nodes.norm_label: assets vs liabilities; cash flow builds wealth

nodes.label: Human nature repeats; incentives drive behavior; resilience over precision
nodes.rationale: Behavioral patterns around money repeat across eras even as tools change; incentives predict behavior more reliably than stated advice. Because forecasts are usually wrong, building margin and resilience matters more than precision, and calm periods can mask growing fragility.
nodes.norm_label: human nature repeats; incentives drive behavior; resilience over precision

nodes.label: Family flexibility and protecting earning power
nodes.rationale: Family plans must absorb caregiving and career transitions, building a bigger margin of safety when others depend on you. Protecting earning power (skills, health, career development) matters as much as protecting savings, and automation keeps saving going despite a busy schedule; emergency target is 3-6 months of essentials.
nodes.norm_label: family flexibility and protecting earning power

nodes.label: Enoughness and values-alignment; self-worth is not net worth
nodes.rationale: Financial success without emotional health can still feel empty; net worth and self-worth are separate measures and conflating them undermines security. Defining 'enough' on your own terms ends endless chasing, and aligning spending with identity and values produces lasting fulfillment.
nodes.norm_label: enoughness and values-alignment; self-worth is not net worth

nodes.label: Money stress is driven by fear, avoidance, and shame
nodes.rationale: Financial stress traces to hidden emotional patterns rather than lack of information; avoidance, emotional spending, fear-based hoarding, and shame-driven secrecy all compound the same underlying fear. Naming a fear and building structure reduces its power more reliably than willpower.
nodes.norm_label: money stress is driven by fear, avoidance, and shame

nodes.label: The behavior gap — knowing is not doing
nodes.rationale: The gap between knowing and doing is where most investing money is lost; emotional reactions like buying high after hype or selling low in panic destroy returns. Simple, automated, rule-based plans are easier to stick with, and the best strategy is the one you can actually follow.
nodes.norm_label: the behavior gap — knowing is not doing

nodes.label: A few good rules followed consistently
nodes.rationale: Most of personal finance rests on a handful of rules, not dozens: save 10-20%, pay cards in full, build 3-6 months reserves, capture the employer match, use low-cost index funds, insure adequately. Fees and complexity are costs not features, and consistency beats optimizing any single rule.
nodes.norm_label: a few good rules followed consistently

nodes.label: Price is not value; margin of safety; temperament over IQ
nodes.rationale: Price is what you pay and value is what you get; a margin of safety (buying below estimated intrinsic value) is the buffer against being wrong. Investing success depends on temperament — emotional control, patience, independence — more than IQ, and panic selling and chasing hot stocks destroy long-term results.
nodes.norm_label: price is not value; margin of safety; temperament over iq

nodes.label: The Little Book of Behavioural Investing
nodes.norm_label: the little book of behavioural investing

nodes.label: Process beats prediction; investors sabotage themselves
nodes.rationale: Investor behavior, not market forecasting, is the biggest lever on long-run returns; overconfidence, herd behavior, and short-termism reliably damage results. A written process (goals, diversification, valuation anchors, rebalancing rules) protects against emotion, and recognizing your biases is the starting point for controlling them.
nodes.norm_label: process beats prediction; investors sabotage themselves

nodes.label: Values-first, simple plan you actually follow
nodes.rationale: A financial plan should start from values and priorities, not market products or optimization; a simple plan you follow beats a perfect plan you abandon. Reviewing on a calm schedule prevents both drift (no written plan) and panic-driven optimization that loses touch with purpose.
nodes.norm_label: values-first, simple plan you actually follow

nodes.label: The Only Investment Guide You'll Ever Need
nodes.norm_label: the only investment guide you'll ever need

nodes.label: Common-sense frugality beats flashy products
nodes.rationale: Spending less than you earn and saving consistently do more for wealth than any product; the ordered playbook (tighten savings, clear expensive debt, build safety net, then invest in diversified low-cost funds) must not be skipped. Complexity is a warning sign, and staying diversified and skeptical of hype protects steady gains.
